The listed-company universe for high-purity K-12 virtual-school suppliers is limited because several directly relevant vendors in SIS, LMS, assessment, curriculum, and special-education compliance are private or no longer straightforward public pure plays.
evidence.source_title: Renaissance K-12 Educational Software Solutions & Learning Analytics

evidence.claim: Frontline-related sources describe special-education and intervention software focused on compliance, IEP workflows, Medicaid billing, and district administrative needs, but Frontline itself is not a public candidate in this US-listed pass.

memory_update.text: LRN should remain the reference demand anchor for K-12 virtual schools and career learning, but should not dominate the underfollowed supplier lane.
NNI/FACTS is a potentially underfollowed K-12 administration, payment, SIS, LMS, enrollment, and funding-workflow supplier hidden inside a broader education-finance company.
EXTR is a second-order education infrastructure candidate through K-12 networking, E-Rate eligibility, online testing, and device-heavy learning environments.
BOXL is a micro-cap speculative shadow candidate only; financial viability and direct virtual-school relevance must be verified before any later-layer survival.

High-relevance K-12 assessment, curriculum, SIS/LMS, special-education compliance, and district workflow suppliers such as Renaissance, Frontline, PowerSchool, and similar platforms appear important for mapping the chokepoint but may be private or taken private, reducing US-listed pure-play availability.

For this node, the likely bottlenecks are not only digital courseware but also state/district authorization, compliance workflows, SIS/LMS reliability, teacher staffing, special-education/IEP processes, connectivity, testing infrastructure, student support, and measurable outcomes.

node: K-12 virtual schools and career-linked online learning
summary: Expanded the universe around the K-12 virtual-school and career-linked learning node with emphasis on regulated workflow infrastructure, K-12 administration/payment rails, network infrastructure, and one visible demand anchor. Public-market scarcity is itself a finding: many high-relevance K-12 curriculum, assessment, SIS, LMS, special-education, and compliance vendors appear private or recently taken private, so the US-listed discovery lane is narrower than the operating ecosystem.
